items.intent: Pick up the spoon and closely examine its edge, rim, and bowl for any signs of sharpening, filing, or deliberate wear — and check the area around where it was resting for metal dust or filings.
Pick up the spoon and closely examine its edge, bowl, and handle for any signs of sharpening, new wear, metal filings, or modification since my last check in round 3.

Walk to the meal tray, pick up the spoon, and examine it closely — specifically checking the worn-flat side of the bowl for any fresh scratching, sharpening, or new wear beyond the baseline. Also glance at Voss's cot area and the blanket as I pass it.

Pick up the spoon from wherever it sits, examine it closely — turning it over, running my thumb along the worn-flat edge to feel for fresh sharpening or new wear — then confiscate it, telling Voss it'll be replaced with a new one at next meal per safety rotation.
Closely examine the bar in the window — run my hands along its full length, check the mortar at top and bottom, and look for any fresh scratches, filing marks, or weakening.
Get my hands on the window bar and inspect the rusted base where it meets the mortar for tool marks or any looseness.
Examine the lock closely — run my fingers along the bolt edge visible in the door gap, inspect the housing for fresh scratch marks, gouges, or metal filings.
Kneel beside the loose tile, lift it out of its seat, and closely examine the hollow beneath for hidden tools or freshly disturbed grit.
Scrape at the cracked mortar around the base of the bar with the spoon.
Drag the spoon's worn-flat edge back and forth along the rough iron crossbar of the cot to sharpen it.
